sections.title: Scenario
sections.prompt: Who is the reviewer for, what does success mean, and which numbers shape the design?
criteria: Defines 'wrong' and 'addressed' precisely enough to measure
Converts 3,000 runs a day into peak runs per minute and GitHub API calls per hour
States that model findings are advisory and do not block merges
Names what the pilot got wrong (volume and nits) as the problem to solve

sections.title: Single View
sections.prompt: Draw the path from a PR event to a posted review.
criteria: Puts a durable queue or workflow between the webhook and the model
Includes a code-context layer beyond the diff (search and code intelligence)
Separates deterministic policy checks from model findings
Includes a ranker that enforces the comment budget after the model

sections.title: Data Sources
sections.prompt: What does a review read, and from where?
criteria: Reads code at the PR head SHA, not only the default branch
Uses a git mirror or clone instead of per-file REST calls
Reads existing linter and CI annotations to avoid duplicates

sections.title: Processing
sections.prompt: How is a run broken into steps, and how are large PRs and re-pushes handled?
criteria: Splits large diffs into groups under a token budget
Reviews only the delta on a new push
Cancels or supersedes in-flight runs for the same PR
Runs policy checks such as secret and migration rules as code

sections.title: Agents
sections.prompt: What do the model calls do, how are they bounded, and what do they cost?
criteria: Separates finding from verifying with evidence
Bounds the tool loop with a call limit
Computes cost per run and per month from token counts and both PR sizes
Routes high-risk paths to a stronger model with a stated share of traffic

sections.title: Memory
sections.prompt: What does the reviewer remember, and who approves what it learns?
criteria: Fingerprints posted comments so dismissed findings do not return
Requires human approval before a learned convention takes effect
Tracks precision per category over time

sections.title: MCP Tool Servers
sections.prompt: What tools can the model call, and what is it denied?
criteria: All code tools are read-only and pinned to the head SHA
Posting comments is done by the orchestrator, not a model tool
Refuses code execution of PR code with the reviewer's credentials
Caps tool result size

sections.title: Endpoints
sections.prompt: What endpoints and GitHub interactions exist, and how is the 5 minute p90 met?
criteria: Verifies webhook signatures and dedupes deliveries
Returns from the webhook quickly and processes asynchronously
Gives a stage-by-stage latency budget under 5 minutes at p90
Posts one review per run rather than one call per comment

sections.title: Caching
sections.prompt: What is cached, and what must the keys include?
criteria: Prompt-caches the shared prefix across verifier calls
Keys any cached findings on content hash and prompt or model version
Keeps warm worktrees or mirrors for active repos

sections.title: Data Stores
sections.prompt: What is stored, how big is it, and what does the system cost per month?
criteria: Sizes mirrors and indexes for the monorepo and service repos
Stores comment outcomes as events for precision analytics
Gives a monthly cost that fits the $60k budget
Sets a short retention for prompts containing source code

sections.title: Output
sections.prompt: What does the author see on the PR?
criteria: Inline comments carry a claim, evidence lines and a category
Enforces a hard maximum of comments per PR with nits off by default
Reports policy results as a check run

sections.title: Guardrails
sections.prompt: What stops the reviewer from doing damage or being manipulated?
criteria: Lists the GitHub App permissions and excludes merge and push
Treats PR content as untrusted and handles prompt injection
Enforces the comment budget in code, not in the prompt
Switches off a category automatically below a precision threshold with a minimum sample

sections.title: Key Impact
sections.prompt: How do you prove the reviewer helps?
criteria: Measures precision by human audit with a stated weekly sample and its confidence interval
Uses a randomized holdout to measure time to merge or reverts
Gives baselines and targets for at least three metrics

sections.title: Failure Modes
sections.prompt: What breaks, and what does the reviewer do when it is degraded?
criteria: Handles the morning burst and the GitHub API limit
Gates prompt and model changes on a labeled offline set
Posts less, not more, when context or the model is degraded

sections.title: Build Order
sections.prompt: How do you roll it out without repeating the pilot?
criteria: Runs in shadow mode and measures precision before posting
Rolls out to volunteer teams before everyone
Ends each phase with a measured number
